The test image shows a tomato leaf with:
- Prominent concentric ring/target-spot patterns across the entire leaf surface
- Chlorotic (yellowish) mottling between rings
- Small necrotic spots scattered throughout
- Some purplish/dark discoloration at the leaf margin

These ring spot patterns are highly characteristic of **Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus (TSWV)**. Let me confirm with one reference image.

The reference shows a more advanced/whole-plant TSWV case. However, the ring spot patterns on the test leaf are the classic early foliar symptom of TSWV — circular concentric rings with chlorotic/mosaic mottling across the leaf. No other class in this list produces that diffuse ring-spot pattern on tomato leaves. Early Blight has similar rings but those are sharply defined dark lesions, not the diffuse virus-type rings seen here.
